articles.title: Why a scrubber has to hold back half a placeholder
articles.focus: Explain the mechanics of streamed rehydration in prompt-scrub v1.5.0: why vendors emit roughly one token per SSE event so a placeholder like «Email_1» genuinely arrives as «Email_ then 1», how the proxy holds a trailing partial placeholder back and joins it to the next fragment, how CRLF/CR/LF event boundaries are detected, and how the held fragment is released on finish_reason or [DONE] so a client that stops reading never loses bytes.

articles.title: Over-redact, never leak: how collision resolution actually works
articles.focus: Show that prompt-scrub v1.5.0's collision resolver narrows a losing finding to the part the winner does not cover rather than dropping it, so an over-broad detector degrades into over-redaction instead of leaking what it over-matched, explain why a narrowed fragment is scored at 0.8 times the original confidence, and cover the O(n log n) rewrite that took a 10,000-finding document from about 1.7 seconds to under 100 milliseconds with byte-identical output.

articles.title: Writing tool schemas that survive a scrubber
articles.focus: Give practitioners a concrete rule of thumb from prompt-scrub v1.5.0: the proxy scrubs free text everywhere but deliberately leaves tool names, tool-call ids, JSON-schema property keys and enum values alone because the model must echo them verbatim for the caller's dispatch to work, and show how the credential-key rule decides what to redact inside tool arguments, treating access_tokens as a secret while leaving max_tokens and generic names like key or auth alone.
